---
title: "Header and footer links"
---

Configure links with Quarto's native navigation options. Askr supplies their
appearance, not a second link registry. The Header offers quick access; the
Footer keeps project, community and maintenance links available after reading.

## Native configuration

```yaml
website:
  navbar:
    tools-collapse: true
    tools:
      - icon: github
        href: https://github.com/your-organization/your-project
        text: GitHub repository
        aria-label: GitHub repository
  page-footer:
    left:
      - icon: github
        aria-label: GitHub repository
        href: https://github.com/your-organization/your-project
      - text: '<i class="bi bi-chat-dots" aria-hidden="true"></i> Community'
        href: https://community.example.org/
    center:
      - text: '<i class="bi bi-book" aria-hidden="true"></i> Maintenance guide'
        href: maintenance.qmd
      - text: '<i class="bi bi-people" aria-hidden="true"></i> Contributing'
        href: contributing.qmd
      - text: '<i class="bi bi-file-earmark-text" aria-hidden="true"></i> License'
        href: license.qmd
      - text: '<i class="bi bi-journal-text" aria-hidden="true"></i> Third-party notices'
        href: THIRD_PARTY.md
    right: "Your project's existing footer content"
```

Replace the example destinations with your own. GitHub appears twice because
these are two native navigation locations; Askr does not synchronize URLs.
Use [Bootstrap icon names](https://icons.getbootstrap.com/) and descriptive
`text` / `aria-label` values. Icon-only Footer links require `aria-label`:
Quarto attaches that name to their native icon. For unfamiliar community links,
a short visible label makes the purpose clearer.
Quarto 1.10.18's Footer text rendering replaces a sibling `icon` when both are
configured, so these examples put decorative Bootstrap icons inside native
`text` markup instead. `aria-hidden` leaves the visible label as the link name.

With `tools-collapse: true`, authored tools move into the
Areas panel when space is insufficient. Theme, Search and optional Logout stay
available in the Header. `false` keeps tools in the Header; use a small set so
they fit your narrowest viewport. Long Footer labels wrap rather than scroll.
Links use Quarto's native `href`, `target` and `rel` behavior; Askr does not force
new browser tabs. Existing links and build information remain authored content.

## Project license and third-party notices

Use ordinary `page-footer` items for your project's license and third-party
notices, alongside its existing project and contribution links. Choose labels
and destinations that match the documents you publish. Askr does not infer
those documents or select a license for a consumer project. The Gallery links
to Askr's own MIT license and asset notices; those are not the license terms
for a site that installs Askr.

Make `license.qmd` a reading page that includes the canonical license file,
rather than copying the legal text into a second source:

```markdown
---
title: "License"
---

The following is this project's canonical license.

{{{< include LICENSE >}}}
```

Footer `href` values in `_quarto.yml` are relative to that Quarto project.
`license.qmd` and `THIRD_PARTY.md` link to their rendered `license.html` and
`THIRD_PARTY.html`; include both sources in the project's render inputs.
Quarto adjusts links for deep pages, so `usage/header-footer.html` links back
to `../license.html` and `../THIRD_PARTY.html`. Project-relative paths also
retain deployment prefixes such as `/docs/` and version directories such as
`/v1.2/`, without baking those directories into each link.

An optional raw `LICENSE` link can offer the original file for download. The
host's content type and response headers determine whether it opens or
downloads, so use the rendered page as the reading entry. If you offer that
raw-file link, include the file in project resources:

```yaml
project:
  resources:
    - LICENSE
```

For separate language projects, each language can have its own reading page
while including the same canonical file. For example, `zh-TW/license.qmd`
uses `{{{< include ../LICENSE >}}}` and explains that the legal text remains in
its original language. Its footer can link to that page and a shared notices
page at the parent site root:

```yaml
website:
  page-footer:
    center:
      - text: 授權條款
        href: license.qmd
      - text: 第三方聲明（英文）
        href: ../THIRD_PARTY.html
```

The parent project renders `THIRD_PARTY.md`. Quarto adjusts the relative paths
again for deeper translated pages. If each language has its own authored
notices, point each project to its own sources instead. Full HTTPS destinations
are also valid when the authoritative document is hosted elsewhere. Existing
GitHub, contribution and maintenance links and the appended Powered by Askr
credit keep their own roles.

## Powered by Askr

The Footer's right section includes `Powered by Askr · version`. Askr links to
its documentation; the version links to its GitHub Release. The installed
extension's `_extension.yml` is the version authority, not `askr-versions.json`
or your document's package version. Unreleased local edits still show their
current package metadata version; this is not proof that those edits shipped.

To omit this credit:

```yaml
askr:
  footer:
    credit: false
```

Askr appends its credit without replacing your right-side content. Without
an authored Footer it creates a minimal credit-only Footer; with credit disabled
it creates nothing. No commit hash is generated or removed by Askr.

See [Quarto's navigation guide](https://quarto.org/docs/websites/website-navigation)
for menus, footer regions and additional native options.
